question: When AI produces scientific results that few people can explain, what should count as real understanding?
reflection: Machines may speed up discovery, but the human work of checking, explaining and sharing knowledge keeps science trustworthy.

sources.subject: China wants a say in who gets AI weights
DeepSeek Flash-1017, Claude Quantum Circuits, Grok Bot 3x Speed

one_line: Governments are starting to treat AI models themselves as controlled exports, just as AI begins to produce science faster than humans can check it.

top_stories.title: China drafts export rules that reach model weights
top_stories.what: China proposed adding 23 AI technologies to its restricted-export list, so sending the most powerful model weights or training methods abroad could need a licence, while API access and open releases would stay largely free.
top_stories.why: If both China and the US control model transfers, organisations that rely on foreign open models for local deployment will face new licensing questions.

top_stories.title: AI starts producing science, not just helping with it
top_stories.what: A leading editorial argues AI is now generating results that reshape fields, citing OpenAI's release of hundreds of papers on hard maths problems, and calls for stronger human review and credit for verifiers.
top_stories.why: Research bodies will need clear rules on how to check, disclose and credit AI-generated findings, which is a governance gap a consultancy can help close.

top_stories.title: Anthropic lets outside evaluators work inside the company
top_stories.what: Anthropic placed six staff from the nonprofit METR inside its offices with near-internal access, and METR can publish findings without company approval, subject to limited redactions.
top_stories.why: This is a practical model for independent auditing that regulators and large AI buyers could ask other vendors to match.

saudi_lens.text: Saudi Arabia builds much of its AI capacity on imported models and chips, so new export rules from China and Taiwan affect which models can legally be deployed on local servers.
As Saudi universities expand AI-driven research, national guidance on verifying and disclosing machine-generated results would protect the credibility of local science.

idea.title: AI research integrity guidelines
idea.pitch: Draft practical guidance for a research funder on when AI-generated findings need human replication, disclosure and peer review.
idea.fit: Government research funding, universities, health research
idea.first_step: Collect three published policies on AI use in research and list where they disagree.

terms.definition: Government rules that limit which goods or technologies can be sold or sent to other countries.
The learned numbers inside an AI model that hold what it has learned; whoever has them can run the model.
Testing of an AI system by an independent group rather than by the company that built it.

concepts.summary: Countries now restrict exports of AI chips and, increasingly, the models themselves.
AI systems producing research results faster than humans can verify them.
Outside groups testing AI systems with real access and freedom to publish.
Firms where agents handle routine work and escalate judgement calls to people.
